chapter: In The Mood, Rendezvous and Capitol
title: The Williams Air Force Base cafe incident
summary: Refused service at an Arizona all-night cafe, trumpeter Wallace Wilson and a white serviceman threaten to tear the place up.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: So anyway, he said, I'll tell you what, after the first of the year, I know to be exact--that was in fifty eight--he said you come on out, we'll get together and do that. So we went on and I think the next thing we were playing was Williams Air Force Base, we were coming on back east, one night, whatever it was, and a little incident happened there.
During our career we had a lot of them, this race deal--
(Side B of Tape 4 ended at this point. Transcript will continue in accordance with Tape 5.)

Yes, Williams Air Force Base in Williams, Arizona. We played the officer's club and we went in and the fans, they were practically hugging and kissing you but when we got through with the dance, everything was closed on the base, so we came on through in the little town and found us an all-night cafe, so we walked in and sat down. We only saw two people in the kitchen, a lady and a man and a white fellow was sitting down eating, he had already been served and we sat and we sat. Nobody came to us and said we're not going to serve you or what will you have, or anything. We just sat there. Finally, this white fellow turned around and said, was anybody here in the Army, in the service? And Wallace Wilson was one-- I think I had two that had been in, I don't know if you knew Wallace Wilson, he was from New York City--I don't know originally but that was where
Trumpet. He was once with Sonny Finnegan, this jazz band, a fine musician.
And so Wallace finally spoke up and he said, and you sit there that long and don't do nothing, he said, let's tear the whole damn joint up.

Then when he said that, the fellow back there said, no, no, don't you all do that, we don't make the laws, and then the white guy said, make the laws, hell, you haven't even thought enough of serve them, what do you think the people came in here for, and he said law, hell, we're going to tear it up or they're going to get some service.
And so the lady walked over (in-audible). He was sitting there all alone and he finally said, has anybody ever been in the
service, and Wallace or somebody spoke up, but I really think it was Wallace in particular and he said you're sitting here this long and don't say anything? He said, let's tear the joint up.
